newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary wants Alitalia to sell Malev stake - paper.
newsitem.headline: Hungary wants Alitalia to sell Malev stake - paper.

text.p: Hungary's state privatisation agency APV Rt wants Italian air carrier Alitalia to pull out of Hungarian national air company Malev Rt, the daily Nepszabadsag said on Monday.

"Malev's current partner, Alitalia, does not belong to any...global alliances nor is the Malev-Alitalia alliance a cooperation ensuring considerable mutual commercial and economic advantages," Nepszabadsag quoted an APV document as saying.
Alitalia in 1993 bought 30 percent of Malev from the state, which still has a 63.9 percent stake.
Nepszabadsag, referring to the recently approved draft strategy for Malev's privatisation, said APV would like Alitalia to sell part or all of its stake at an early stage of the privatisation.
Nepszabadsag said the government was likely to approve the draft at its meeting on January 9.
APV declined to comment on the newspaper report.
APV's believed the best solution for Malev would be for it to join one of the global cooperation groups of air carriers, to which Alitalia did not belong, the newspaper said.
"The aim is that conforming to the trend, Malev should join an existing or future global alliance," it added.
Nepszabadsag said that according to the APV draft, the state planned to remain the main shareholder in Malev in 1997, but that financial investors should raise the company's capital next year.
The state plans to sell shares in Malev through a tender to strategic investors in 1998. Later Hungarian institutional investors would raise the issued share capital again.
The privatisation would be followed by listing of Malev shares on the Budapest Stock Exchange.

The state plans to retain 25 percent plus one share in Malev and to sell 25 percent to domestic investors so as to maintain a Hungarian majority as the status of 'national air carrier' offered certain advantages, Nepszabadsag said.
